subject.title: Cron jobs stall during AI model calls (model_call:stream_progress never completes)

question: Should this issue remain the canonical tracker for the remaining `cron.wake mode:"now"` success-vs-failure contract, or should maintainers split that into a focused issue and close this bundle after the next-release retest?
rationale: The model-call stall is fixed on main, but the remaining behavior is a Gateway/cron API contract choice: whether fire-and-forget wake success means enqueue accepted or should reflect the later heartbeat outcome.

options.title: Split the wake contract
options.body: Open or designate a focused tracker for `cron.wake mode:"now"` result semantics, then close this bundled issue after PR 102160 ships and Bug 1/Bug 2 are retested.

options.title: Keep this issue scoped to Bug 3
options.body: Leave this issue open as the canonical remaining tracker but update the title/body scope to avoid re-litigating the fixed stream-stall path.

options.title: Accept fire-and-forget semantics
options.body: Document that `cron.wake` success only means the wake was enqueued and close the remaining Bug 3 as expected behavior if maintainers choose that contract.

recommendation.title: Split the wake contract
recommendation.body: Open or designate a focused tracker for `cron.wake mode:"now"` result semantics, then close this bundled issue after PR 102160 ships and Bug 1/Bug 2 are retested.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus authored the merged reliability stack and already summarized the current fixed-versus-remaining scope on this issue.
